text:
PhonePe, CRED, Groww and Razorpay have one investor in common: Ribbit Capital, a Silicon Valley fund that invests only in fintech.

Ribbit isn't the only one. Fintech-only funds from the US, Europe and Asia keep writing cheques into Indian startups, from pre-seed cohorts to $20M growth rounds.

In this carousel: 8 global fintech investors that back Indian founders. It covers Tenity, Coinbase Ventures, Saison Capital, Flourish, QED, Quona, Ribbit and FinSight, with stage, cheque size, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: specialist fintech investors already know your regulator, your unit economics and your competitors. Lead with the numbers they will ask for first: credit losses, take rate, CAC payback and your licence or partner-bank setup. And match the fund to your stage: Tenity and Coinbase Ventures write early cheques, while Ribbit and FinSight usually come in once traction is proven.

investors.stage: Pre-seed (VC arm up to Series A)

investors.name: Coinbase Ventures
investors.note: Fits if your product runs on on-chain rails, like cross-border stablecoin payments.

investors.name: Saison Capital
investors.note: Venture arm of a Japanese lender, so it understands credit and NBFC-style models.

investors.name: Flourish Ventures
investors.note: Leads rounds in India. Show how you improve customers' financial health, not just growth.

investors.name: QED Investors
investors.note: Operator-heavy team putting $250-300M to work across India and APAC.

investors.name: Quona Capital
investors.note: Has a Bengaluru team. Best fit if you serve underserved MSMEs or consumers.

investors.name: Ribbit Capital
investors.note: Very selective; usually comes in once traction is clear. Pitch with category-leader data.

investors.name: FinSight Ventures
investors.note: Plans to deploy $150-160M in India over 2-3 years. Approach once revenue is proven.

text:
Bengaluru rocket startup EtherealX has raised a $20.5M Series A. Before that, it was in the first India cohort of Accel's Atoms pre-seed programme.

Global accelerators are still one of the fastest ways for an Indian founder to get a first cheque, credits and a network abroad. Many of them now have India cohorts or actively take Indian teams.

In this carousel: 8 global accelerators and startup programmes open to Indian founders. It covers Founder Institute, Accel Atoms, Techstars, 500 Global, Microsoft for Startups, UChicago's India Deep Tech Accelerator, Stanford Seed Spark and the AWS Generative AI Accelerator, with what you get, Indian alumni and how to apply.

Quick tip: read the terms before you apply. Some programmes take equity (Techstars, 500 Global), some give only credits (Microsoft, AWS), and some need a partner incubator to nominate you (Stanford Seed Spark). Pick the one that fills your real gap, whether that is money, customers or a US market entry.

investors.name: Founder Institute
investors.note: Low-cost way to test an idea. Mumbai and Hyderabad cohorts close 15 Dec 2026.

investors.note: Rolling applications. Open to Indian-origin founders anywhere, even before incorporation.

investors.name: Techstars
investors.note: No India programme now, but Indian teams still get into flagship US programmes.

investors.name: 500 Global
investors.cheque: Up to $50K upfront; up to $1M follow-on
investors.note: 4 months in-person in San Francisco. Best for India-built teams targeting the US.

investors.name: Microsoft for Startups
investors.note: Sign up for credits from day one; India cohorts like UNNATI AI add mentoring.

investors.name: UChicago India Deep Tech Accel.
investors.note: Built for IIT and research spinouts heading to the US. Watch for the next cohort call.

investors.name: Stanford Seed Spark
investors.note: No direct applications: a partner incubator nominates you. Ask yours if it is one.

investors.name: AWS Generative AI Accelerator
investors.note: Fits compute-heavy AI teams. Indian startups made the 2024 and 2025 global cohorts.
